name: Customer Identification Policy
description: FirstUK Bank's formal policy governing customer identification and Know Your Customer (KYC) procedures. The policy is owned by the Head of Compliance and applies to all staff, branch managers, compliance, and risk personnel. It is mandated by FCA COBS Part 10 and the Money Laundering Regulations 2017, and was effective from 2026-01-15 with a scheduled review date of 2027-01-15.
context: Regulatory Reference | FCA COBS Part 10, Money Laundering Regulations 2017
Audience | All Staff, Branch Managers, Compliance, Risk

name: FCA COBS Part 10
description: Financial Conduct Authority regulation governing conduct of business rules, specifically Part 10, which addresses customer identification and Know Your Customer requirements. This regulation mandates the Customer Identification Policy.
context: Regulatory Reference | FCA COBS Part 10, Money Laundering Regulations 2017

name: Money Laundering Regulations 2017
description: UK legislation establishing anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing obligations, including customer identification and due diligence requirements. This regulation mandates the Customer Identification Policy.
context: Regulatory Reference | FCA COBS Part 10, Money Laundering Regulations 2017

name: Head of Compliance
description: The designated policy owner responsible for the Customer Identification Policy. The Head of Compliance holds accountability for policy governance, maintenance, and compliance oversight.

name: All Staff
description: All employees of FirstUK Bank are identified as an audience for the Customer Identification Policy, indicating that customer identification obligations apply across the entire organisation.
context: Audience | All Staff, Branch Managers, Compliance, Risk

name: Branch Managers
description: Branch managers are identified as a key audience for the Customer Identification Policy, with responsibility for ensuring compliance at branch level.
context: Audience | All Staff, Branch Managers, Compliance, Risk

name: Compliance
description: The Compliance function is identified as both the policy owner department and a key audience for the Customer Identification Policy, responsible for policy implementation and oversight.
context: Audience | All Staff, Branch Managers, Compliance, Risk

name: Risk
description: The Risk function is identified as an audience for the Customer Identification Policy, indicating involvement in risk assessment and monitoring of customer identification compliance.
context: Audience | All Staff, Branch Managers, Compliance, Risk

name: Customer Identification Policy
description: FirstUK Bank's comprehensive policy establishing mandatory procedures for verifying customer identity and address at account opening and periodically thereafter. The policy is designed to ensure customer legitimacy, prevent financial crime, and comply with regulatory requirements.
context: FirstUK Bank maintains a comprehensive Customer Identification Policy (KYC)
This policy establishes mandatory procedures for verifying customer identity and address at account opening and periodically thereafter
ensure customer legitimacy, prevent financial crime, and comply with regulatory requirements

name: Mandatory Identity Verification at Account Opening
description: A core requirement of the Customer Identification Policy mandating that customer identity must be verified at the point of account opening as part of the KYC process.
context: mandatory procedures for verifying customer identity and address at account opening

name: Periodic Address Verification
description: A requirement under the Customer Identification Policy to verify customer address not only at account opening but also periodically throughout the customer relationship.
context: verifying customer identity and address at account opening and periodically thereafter

name: Financial Crime
description: A broad risk category that the Customer Identification Policy is designed to prevent through mandatory customer verification procedures. The policy treats financial crime prevention as a core objective alongside regulatory compliance.
context: ensure customer legitimacy, prevent financial crime, and comply with regulatory requirements

name: Identity Verification
description: The process of verifying customer identity as mandated by FirstUK Bank's Customer Identification Policy, performed at account opening and periodically thereafter as part of the bank's KYC obligations.
context: verifying customer identity and address at account opening and periodically thereafter
mandatory procedures for verifying customer identity

name: Address Verification
description: The process of verifying customer address as mandated by FirstUK Bank's Customer Identification Policy, performed at account opening and periodically thereafter as part of the bank's KYC obligations.
context: verifying customer identity and address at account opening and periodically thereafter
mandatory procedures for verifying customer identity and address

name: Know Your Customer Verification Policy
description: A formal policy establishing procedures for Know Your Customer verification to confirm customer identity, verify address, assess risk profile, and meet FCA COBS and Money Laundering Regulations requirements. The policy is designed to prevent opening accounts for sanctioned individuals or entities.
context: To establish procedures for Know Your Customer (KYC) verification that: Confirm customer identity, Verify customer address, Assess customer risk profile, Meet FCA COBS and Money Laundering Regulations requirements, Prevent opening accounts for sanctioned individuals or entities

name: Customer Identity Confirmation
description: A mandatory requirement to confirm the identity of customers as part of the KYC verification process.

name: Customer Address Verification
description: A mandatory requirement to verify the address of customers as part of the KYC verification process.

name: Customer Risk Profile Assessment
description: A mandatory requirement to assess the risk profile of customers as part of the KYC verification process.

name: Prohibition on Account Opening for Sanctioned Individuals or Entities
description: A prohibition against opening accounts for sanctioned individuals or entities, enforced through KYC verification procedures.
context: Prevent opening accounts for sanctioned individuals or entities

name: FCA COBS Requirements
description: The Financial Conduct Authority's Conduct of Business sourcebook, which establishes regulatory requirements that the KYC policy must meet.
context: Meet FCA COBS and Money Laundering Regulations requirements

name: Money Laundering Regulations
description: The Money Laundering Regulations that establish anti-money laundering and KYC requirements that the policy must comply with.
context: Meet FCA COBS and Money Laundering Regulations requirements

name: Sanctions Violation
description: The risk that the bank may inadvertently open accounts for sanctioned individuals or entities, which the KYC policy is designed to prevent.
context: Prevent opening accounts for sanctioned individuals or entities

name: Money Laundering
description: The risk of money laundering, which the KYC verification procedures are designed to mitigate through customer identity confirmation, address verification, and risk profile assessment.
context: Meet FCA COBS and Money Laundering Regulations requirements

name: Identity Verification
description: The process of verifying customer identity as a core component of the KYC verification procedure.

name: Address Verification
description: The process of verifying customer address as a core component of the KYC verification procedure.

name: Customer Account Opening and KYC Verification Policy
description: Policy governing the scope and application of customer account opening procedures and Know Your Customer verification requirements. Establishes mandatory KYC processes for retail and joint account openings, new customer relationships, and periodic re-verification activities. Defines staff responsibilities in customer onboarding and specifies exclusions for existing customers, regulatory authorities, and internal bank accounts.
context: Applies to: All customer account openings (retail, joint accounts)
All staff involved in customer onboarding

name: Mandatory KYC Verification at Account Opening
description: Requires KYC verification to be performed for all retail and joint account openings and new customer relationships. This is a core compliance obligation that must be completed before account activation.
context: Applies to: All customer account openings (retail, joint accounts)

name: Periodic KYC Re-verification Requirement
description: Mandates periodic re-verification of customer KYC information at defined intervals as specified in the business ontology KYC Verification entity. This ensures ongoing compliance and risk management for existing customer relationships.

name: Staff Responsibility for Customer Onboarding
description: Establishes that all staff involved in customer onboarding are subject to and responsible for implementing the KYC verification requirements defined in this policy.
context: All staff involved in customer onboarding

name: Exclusion of Existing Customers from Routine KYC
description: Specifies that existing customers are not subject to routine KYC verification unless a risk reassessment is triggered. This provision establishes the boundary between new customer onboarding and ongoing customer management.
context: Does not apply to: Existing customers (unless triggered by risk reassessment)

name: Exclusion of Regulatory Authorities from KYC Requirements
description: Exempts regulatory authorities from KYC verification requirements under this policy.
context: Does not apply to: Regulatory authorities

name: Exclusion of Internal Bank Accounts from KYC Requirements
description: Exempts internal bank accounts from KYC verification requirements under this policy.
context: Does not apply to: Internal bank accounts

name: KYC Verification
description: The Know Your Customer verification process required at account opening and periodically thereafter. Applies to all retail and joint account openings and new customer relationships as a mandatory compliance control.
context: All customer account openings (retail, joint accounts)

name: Retail Account
description: A retail customer account subject to KYC verification requirements at opening and periodic re-verification as defined in this policy.
context: All customer account openings (retail, joint accounts)

name: Joint Account
description: A joint account held by multiple customers subject to KYC verification requirements at opening and periodic re-verification as defined in this policy.
context: All customer account openings (retail, joint accounts)

name: New Customer
description: A customer entering into a new relationship with the bank and opening an account. Subject to mandatory KYC verification before account activation.
context: All customer account openings (retail, joint accounts)

name: Existing Customer
description: A customer with an established relationship with the bank. Exempt from routine KYC verification unless a risk reassessment is triggered.
context: Does not apply to: Existing customers (unless triggered by risk reassessment)

name: Customer Onboarding Staff
description: All staff members involved in the customer account opening and onboarding process. Responsible for implementing and executing KYC verification requirements as defined in this policy.
context: All staff involved in customer onboarding

name: Customer Identification and Verification Policy
description: FirstUK Bank's foundational policy requiring positive identification and verification of all customers prior to account opening or product provision. This policy establishes the bank's mandatory stance on customer due diligence at the point of relationship initiation.
context: FirstUK Bank requires that all customers be positively identified and verified before account opening or product provision.

name: Mandatory Positive Customer Identification Before Account Opening
description: A binding requirement that all customers must be positively identified prior to account opening. This provision establishes the operational gate that must be satisfied before any account can be established.
context: all customers be positively identified and verified before account opening or product provision

name: Mandatory Customer Verification Before Product Provision
description: A binding requirement that all customers must be verified prior to the provision of any banking product. This provision ensures compliance with due diligence obligations at the point of product delivery.
context: all customers be positively identified and verified before account opening or product provision

name: Customer Identity Verification
description: The process of positively identifying customers as mandated by FirstUK Bank policy. This verification must be completed before account opening or product provision can proceed.
context: all customers be positively identified and verified before account opening or product provision

name: Customer
description: Any natural person seeking to open an account or receive a banking product from FirstUK Bank, subject to mandatory identification and verification requirements prior to relationship initiation.
context: all customers be positively identified and verified before account opening or product provision

name: Account
description: A banking account to be opened by a customer, which cannot be established until the customer has been positively identified and verified in accordance with policy requirements.
context: before account opening or product provision

name: Banking Product
description: Any banking product offered by FirstUK Bank that cannot be provided to a customer until positive identification and verification have been completed.
context: before account opening or product provision

name: Mandatory Identity Verification at Account Opening
description: A mandatory requirement that identity verification must be performed at the point of account opening. This is a core Know Your Customer obligation applicable to all new accounts.
context: Identity Verification: Mandatory at account opening

name: Mandatory Address Verification at Account Opening
description: A mandatory requirement that address verification must be performed at the point of account opening. This is a core Know Your Customer obligation applicable to all new accounts.
context: Address Verification: Mandatory at account opening

name: Physical Evidence Documentation Requirement
description: A mandatory requirement that physical evidence must be obtained and retained as part of the identity and address verification process. This ensures documentary proof of customer identity and address.

name: Record Retention for Six Years Post-Account Closure
description: A mandatory record retention requirement that all KYC documentation and account records must be retained for a period of six years following account closure. This ensures compliance with regulatory record-keeping obligations.

name: Periodic KYC Review for Lower-Risk Customers
description: A mandatory periodic review requirement that lower-risk customers must have their KYC information reviewed every 3 to 5 years. This ensures ongoing compliance with Know Your Customer obligations for lower-risk customer segments.
context: Periodic Review: Every 3–5 years for lower-risk customers

name: Periodic KYC Review for High-Risk Customers
description: A mandatory periodic review requirement that high-risk customers must have their KYC information reviewed annually. This ensures enhanced ongoing compliance monitoring for customers presenting elevated risk profiles.

name: Exception Process Escalation to Compliance Head
description: A mandatory requirement that non-standard KYC scenarios must be escalated to the Compliance Head for approval and exception handling. This ensures senior oversight of cases that do not fit standard verification procedures.
context: Exception Process: Escalation to Compliance Head for non-standard scenarios

name: Identity Verification
description: The Know Your Customer process of verifying a customer's identity at account opening. This is a mandatory control performed on all new accounts to establish the true identity of the account holder.
context: Identity Verification: Mandatory at account opening

name: Address Verification
description: The Know Your Customer process of verifying a customer's address at account opening. This is a mandatory control performed on all new accounts to confirm the residential or business address of the account holder.
context: Address Verification: Mandatory at account opening

name: Periodic KYC Refresh
description: The ongoing Know Your Customer process of periodically reviewing and refreshing customer identity and address information. The frequency varies by risk profile: every 3–5 years for lower-risk customers and annually for high-risk customers.
context: Periodic Review: Every 3–5 years for lower-risk customers; annually for high-risk customers

name: High-Risk Customer
description: A customer classification indicating elevated compliance risk requiring enhanced due diligence and more frequent KYC review. High-risk customers are subject to annual KYC periodic reviews rather than the standard 3–5 year cycle.

name: Lower-Risk Customer
description: A customer classification indicating lower compliance risk requiring standard due diligence procedures. Lower-risk customers are subject to KYC periodic reviews on a 3–5 year cycle.

name: Compliance Head
description: A senior compliance role responsible for approving and handling exceptions to standard KYC procedures. The Compliance Head has authority to escalate and approve non-standard verification scenarios.
context: Escalation to Compliance Head for non-standard scenarios

name: Identity Verification Procedures
description: Policy governing the acceptable identity documents and verification methods for UK and non-UK customers during the KYC process. Specifies document types, validity requirements, and verification mechanisms including direct examination, certified copies, and DVLA online checks.
context: Verification method: Direct examination or certified copy

name: UK Passport
description: Valid, non-expired UK passport accepted as primary identity document for UK customers. Document verification includes examination of signature, photo, and personal details through direct examination or certified copy.
context: Document check: Signature, photo, personal details
Verification method: Direct examination or certified copy

name: UK Driving License
description: Valid, non-expired UK photocard driving license accepted as primary identity document for UK customers. Document verification includes photo, signature, address, and driving record checks via DVLA online verification.
context: UK Driving License — Valid, not expired, photocard
Document check: Photo, signature, address, driving record

name: UK National ID Card
description: Valid, non-expired UK National ID Card accepted as primary identity document for UK customers when introduced. Conditional acceptance pending formal introduction of this document type.
context: UK National ID Card — Valid, not expired (when introduced)

name: Foreign Passport
description: Foreign passport from English-speaking countries accepted as primary identity document for non-UK customers. Preference given to passports from English-speaking jurisdictions.

name: EU Driving License
description: EU-equivalent driving license accepted as primary identity document for non-UK customers. Equivalent to UK photocard driving license in terms of acceptable verification standards.

name: EU National ID Card
description: EU-equivalent national ID card accepted as primary identity document for non-UK customers. Equivalent to UK national ID card standards.

name: Direct Examination of Identity Documents
description: Verification method requiring direct physical examination of identity documents by bank staff. Applicable to UK passports and driving licenses as part of the primary KYC verification process.
context: Verification method: Direct examination or certified copy

name: Certified Copy Identity Document Verification
description: Verification method accepting certified copies of identity documents as an alternative to direct examination. Applicable to UK passports and driving licenses during the KYC process.
context: Verification method: Direct examination or certified copy

name: DVLA Online Verification
description: Online verification method using DVLA (Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency) systems to verify UK driving licenses. Checks photo, signature, address, and driving record details.

name: UK Customer
description: Customer resident in or domiciled in the United Kingdom subject to UK-specific identity verification requirements. Must provide valid UK passport, UK driving license, or UK national ID card.
context: UK Driving License — Valid, not expired, photocard

name: Non-UK Customer
description: Customer resident outside the United Kingdom subject to alternative identity verification requirements. May provide foreign passport from English-speaking countries, EU-equivalent driving license, or EU-equivalent national ID card.

name: Customer Identification Process
description: A four-step customer identification procedure encompassing document collection, physical verification, system recording, and channel-specific verification methods. The process requires examination of primary identification documents, assessment of document integrity, photo matching, and signature verification, with different assurance levels applied based on the account opening channel (branch, online, or postal).
context: Examine original document in person (branch opening) or certified copy (postal)
Verify photo matches customer appearance (if in-person)
Record document type, number, issue/expiry dates in AMS (Account Management System)

name: Primary Identification Document
description: The main identity document collected from the customer during account opening, subject to integrity assessment, expiry verification, and recording in the Account Management System. The document must be examined for tampering or alterations and linked to the customer record.
context: Collect document ID, issue date, expiry date

name: Certified Copy
description: A notarized or certified copy of the primary identification document submitted by customers opening accounts online or via postal channels. Certified copies are subject to automated validation and manual review by Compliance staff.
context: Examine original document in person (branch opening) or certified copy (postal)
Customer sends certified copy by registered mail

name: Document Integrity Assessment
description: A control measure requiring staff to assess identification documents for signs of tampering, alterations, or damage during the document collection phase. This assessment is performed as part of Step 1 of the identification process.
context: Examine original document in person (branch opening) or certified copy (postal)

name: Photo Matching Verification
description: A control measure requiring staff to verify that the photograph on the identification document matches the customer's appearance during in-person branch opening. This verification is performed as part of Step 2 of the identification process.
context: Verify photo matches customer appearance (if in-person)

name: Signature Verification
description: A control measure requiring staff to verify that the signature on the identification document matches the customer's specimen signature. This verification is performed as part of Step 2 of the identification process.

name: Document Expiry Verification
description: A control measure requiring staff to confirm that the identification document has not expired before accepting it for KYC purposes. This verification is performed as part of Step 2 of the identification process.
context: Collect document ID, issue date, expiry date

name: Account Management System Recording
description: A control measure requiring staff to record identification document details (type, number, issue and expiry dates) in the Account Management System and link the document to the customer's identification record. Any concerns identified during verification are flagged for manual review.
context: Record document type, number, issue/expiry dates in AMS (Account Management System)
Flag any concerns for manual review

name: Automated Document Validation
description: An optional automated control measure available for online account openings to validate certified copies of identification documents before manual review by Compliance staff.

name: Address Verification Cross-Reference
description: A control measure requiring staff to cross-reference the customer's address with the identification document during postal account opening verification. This is performed as part of the postal verification channel procedure.

name: Follow-Up Verification Call
description: A recommended control measure for postal account openings involving a follow-up verification call to the customer to confirm identity and address details. This provides additional assurance for lower-assurance postal opening channels.

name: Branch Staff
description: Staff members responsible for conducting in-person identification verification during branch account openings. Their responsibilities include examining original documents, verifying photo matches, checking signatures, and recording verification details with their name and date.

name: Compliance Staff
description: Staff members responsible for manual review of identification documents submitted through online and postal account opening channels. They conduct document validation, flag concerns for escalation, and record verification details with their name and date.

name: Branch Account Opening
description: An account opening conducted in person at a branch location, subject to the highest assurance identification verification procedures including physical examination of original documents and immediate in-person photo and signature verification.

name: Online Account Opening
description: An account opening conducted through an online channel, subject to medium assurance identification verification procedures including customer upload of certified copies and automated or manual document validation by Compliance staff.

name: Postal Account Opening
description: An account opening conducted via postal submission, subject to lower assurance identification verification procedures including manual review of certified copies, address cross-reference, and recommended follow-up verification calls.
context: Customer sends certified copy by registered mail

name: Address Verification
description: The process of verifying a customer's address using acceptable documentary evidence. The policy establishes a tiered approach with primary preferred documents (utility bills, council tax documents, bank statements) and secondary alternatives when primary documents are unavailable. All primary documents must be current and match the customer's name and address.
context: Primary (Preferred): Utility Bill — Gas, electricity, water, telephone
Requirement: Current bill (dated within last 3 months)
Check: Matches customer name and address

name: Utility Bill
description: An acceptable primary address verification document covering gas, electricity, water, or telephone bills. Must be current (dated within the last 3 months), match the customer's name and address, and be issued by a major supplier only.
context: Utility Bill — Gas, electricity, water, telephone
Requirement: Current bill (dated within last 3 months)
Check: Matches customer name and address

name: Council Tax Document
description: An acceptable primary address verification document comprising a council tax bill or banding notice. Must be from the current year and match the customer's name and address.
context: Council Tax Document — Council tax bill or banding notice

name: Bank Statement
description: An acceptable primary address verification document from another bank. Must be current (within 3 months) and show the customer's name and address. Cannot be accepted as sole evidence if the customer holds an account with the bank conducting the verification.
context: Limitation: Not accepted as sole evidence if customer has account with us

name: Mortgage Statement
description: An acceptable secondary address verification document used when primary documents are unavailable.

name: Tenancy Agreement
description: An acceptable secondary address verification document. Must be signed and include landlord details.

name: Insurance Policy
description: An acceptable secondary address verification document covering buildings or contents insurance policies.

name: HM Revenue & Customs Correspondence
description: An acceptable secondary address verification document comprising official correspondence from HM Revenue & Customs.

name: Electoral Register Extract
description: An acceptable secondary address verification document comprising an extract from the electoral register.

name: Primary Document Acceptance Requirement
description: Mandates that primary address verification documents (utility bills, council tax documents, or bank statements) must be current and match the customer's name and address exactly.
context: Check: Matches customer name and address
Requirement: Current bill (dated within last 3 months)

name: Bank Statement Sole Evidence Prohibition
description: Prohibits the acceptance of a bank statement as sole evidence of address verification if the customer holds an account with the bank conducting the verification.
context: Limitation: Not accepted as sole evidence if customer has account with us

name: Utility Bill Currency Requirement
description: Requires that utility bills used for address verification must be dated within the last 3 months.
context: Requirement: Current bill (dated within last 3 months)

name: Council Tax Document Currency Requirement
description: Requires that council tax documents used for address verification must be from the current year.
context: Council Tax Document — Council tax bill or banding notice

name: Bank Statement Currency Requirement
description: Requires that bank statements used for address verification must be current (dated within 3 months).

name: Major Supplier Requirement for Utility Bills
description: Mandates that utility bills accepted for address verification must be issued by major suppliers only.

name: Signed Tenancy Agreement with Landlord Details
description: Requires that tenancy agreements used as secondary address verification documents must be signed and include landlord details.

name: Address Verification Process
description: A three-step Know Your Customer process for verifying customer address information. The process involves collecting address verification documents, comparing addresses across ID and supporting documents, confirming UK or approved jurisdiction residency, and recording results in the system with flagging of discrepancies.
context: Compare address on ID document with address on supporting document
Confirm address is within UK (or approved jurisdiction)
Record address document type and date in system

name: Address Verification Document
description: A supporting document used to verify a customer's address during the KYC process. The document type and date are recorded and compared against the address shown on the customer's ID document.
context: Record document type, date, address shown
Compare address on ID document with address on supporting document

name: ID Document
description: An official identity document containing the customer's address, used as the primary reference point in address verification. The address shown on the ID document is compared against supporting address verification documents.
context: Compare address on ID document with address on supporting document
Record document type, date, address shown

name: Address Discrepancy Flagging
description: A control mechanism that flags any discrepancies identified during the address verification process. Discrepancies between ID document address and supporting document address are recorded in the system for review and investigation.

name: UK Postcode Format Validation
description: A validation control that confirms the address postcode conforms to the UK postcode format specification A(1,2)9(1,2)A 9A(2). This ensures address data quality and confirms UK residency or approved jurisdiction status.
context: Confirm address is within UK (or approved jurisdiction)

name: Address System Recording
description: A system-based control that records address verification document type and date, and links the verified address to the business ontology Address entity. This ensures audit trail and data integrity for address verification outcomes.
context: Record address document type and date in system

name: Low Risk Customer
description: Customer profile characterised by age 18–65, UK nationality, UK address, standard product usage, absence of adverse media, non-PEP status, and no high-value transactions. Represents the baseline risk tier for customer assessment.
context: Low Risk: Age 18–65, UK national, UK address, Standard products (savings, current account), No adverse media, Not PEP, No high-value transactions

name: Medium Risk Customer
description: Customer profile characterised by age outside standard range (>65 or <18, with >16 allowed for limited products), non-UK residence with UK citizenship, higher-value accounts exceeding £100k, professional or business customer status, or minor PEP connections.
context: Medium Risk: Age >65 or <18 (>16 allowed for limited products), Non-UK resident but UK citizen, Higher-value account (>£100k), Professional or business customer, Minor PEP connections

name: High Risk Customer
description: Customer profile characterised by non-UK citizenship with foreign address, significant PEP exposure, unclear beneficial ownership, transaction patterns suggesting elevated risk, residence in OFAC/sanctions-listed countries, identified adverse media, or compliance referral.
context: High Risk: Non-UK citizen with foreign address, Significant PEP exposure, Beneficial owner unclear, Transaction pattern suggests higher risk, Country of residence on OFAC/sanctions list, Adverse media identified, Referred by Compliance

name: Savings Account Product
description: Standard savings product referenced as a low-risk product category in the risk-based customer assessment framework.

name: Current Account Product
description: Standard current account product referenced as a low-risk product category in the risk-based customer assessment framework.

name: PEP Screening
description: Politically Exposed Person screening obligation integrated into risk-based customer assessment. Customers with no PEP status are classified as low risk, minor PEP connections elevate to medium risk, and significant PEP exposure triggers high-risk classification.

name: Adverse Media Check
description: Adverse media screening obligation integrated into risk-based customer assessment. Absence of adverse media is a low-risk indicator, while identified adverse media triggers high-risk classification.

name: OFAC Sanctions List Screening
description: Sanctions screening obligation requiring assessment of customer country of residence against OFAC and other sanctions lists. Residence in a sanctions-listed country is a high-risk indicator.
context: Country of residence on OFAC/sanctions list

name: Individual Customer
description: Natural person subject to risk-based customer assessment framework. Risk classification determines the intensity of due diligence, monitoring, and ongoing compliance obligations.

name: Professional or Business Customer
description: Customer engaged in professional or business activities, classified as medium risk under the risk-based assessment framework.

name: Beneficial Owner
description: Ultimate beneficial owner of an account or customer relationship. Unclear beneficial ownership is a high-risk indicator requiring enhanced due diligence.

name: Risk-Based Customer Assessment
description: Structured Know Your Customer assessment process that categorises customers into low, medium, or high risk tiers based on demographic, geographic, product, transaction, and compliance factors. Assessment determines the scope and intensity of ongoing due diligence obligations.

name: High-Value Transaction
description: Transaction activity referenced as a risk indicator. Absence of high-value transactions is a low-risk indicator, while higher-value accounts exceeding £100k elevate risk classification.

name: Transaction Pattern Assessment
description: Ongoing assessment of customer transaction patterns as part of risk-based customer evaluation. Transaction patterns suggesting higher risk trigger high-risk classification.

name: Risk-Based Re-verification Policy
description: A policy establishing a risk-based schedule for periodic re-verification of customer identity and address information. Re-verification frequency is tiered according to customer risk classification, ranging from every 5 years for low-risk customers to annual or on-transaction basis for high-risk customers.

name: Low-Risk Customer Re-verification Frequency
description: Mandatory requirement that customers classified as low-risk must undergo re-verification of identity and address information every 5 years.

name: Medium-Risk Customer Re-verification Frequency
description: Mandatory requirement that customers classified as medium-risk must undergo re-verification of identity and address information every 3 years.

name: High-Risk Customer Re-verification Frequency
description: Mandatory requirement that customers classified as high-risk must undergo re-verification of identity and address information annually or on a per-transaction basis.

name: Customer Risk Classification
description: A risk categorisation framework used to determine the frequency and intensity of customer re-verification obligations. The policy defines three risk tiers: low, medium, and high, each with corresponding re-verification schedules.

name: Periodic Identity and Address Re-verification
description: The ongoing process of re-verifying customer identity and address information at intervals determined by the customer's risk classification. This control ensures that customer information remains current and accurate throughout the customer lifecycle.

name: Low-Risk Customer
description: A customer classified as presenting low compliance risk, subject to re-verification of identity and address information every 5 years under the risk-based re-verification policy.

name: Medium-Risk Customer
description: A customer classified as presenting medium compliance risk, subject to re-verification of identity and address information every 3 years under the risk-based re-verification policy.

name: High-Risk Customer
description: A customer classified as presenting high compliance risk, subject to re-verification of identity and address information annually or on a per-transaction basis under the risk-based re-verification policy.

name: Enhanced Due Diligence Policy
description: Policy mandating Enhanced Due Diligence procedures for high-risk customers and specific trigger scenarios. Establishes mandatory verification procedures, escalation requirements, and ongoing monitoring obligations for customers presenting elevated compliance risk.
context: Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) Mandatory for high-risk customers and certain scenarios

EDD Procedures: 1. Enhanced identity verification (multiple documents) 2. Beneficial ownership verification (if customer is entity) 3. Source of funds verification 4. Ongoing transaction monitoring 5. Periodic review (annual minimum) 6. Documentation of risk assessment
Escalation: Compliance Head approval required for EDD customers

name: Enhanced Identity Verification for High-Risk Customers
description: Requires collection and verification of multiple identity documents for customers triggering EDD procedures. This is a core procedural control within the Enhanced Due Diligence framework.

name: Beneficial Ownership Verification for Entity Customers
description: Mandates verification of beneficial ownership structure when the customer is a legal entity rather than an individual. Required as part of EDD procedures.
context: Beneficial ownership verification (if customer is entity)

name: Source of Funds Verification
description: Requires verification of the origin and legitimacy of customer funds as part of Enhanced Due Diligence procedures for high-risk customers.

name: Ongoing Transaction Monitoring for EDD Customers
description: Establishes requirement for continuous monitoring of transactions for customers subject to Enhanced Due Diligence, as part of ongoing compliance obligations.

name: Periodic EDD Review
description: Mandates periodic review of Enhanced Due Diligence assessments for high-risk customers at a minimum annual frequency to ensure continued appropriateness of risk classification.

name: Documentation of Risk Assessment
description: Requires formal documentation and retention of risk assessments conducted for Enhanced Due Diligence customers, creating an audit trail of compliance decisions.

name: Compliance Head Approval for EDD Customers
description: Mandates that the Compliance Head must provide explicit approval before a customer is classified as requiring Enhanced Due Diligence procedures.
context: Escalation: Compliance Head approval required for EDD customers

name: High-Risk Country Exposure
description: Risk category identifying customers domiciled in or conducting business from jurisdictions designated as high-risk for money laundering, terrorist financing, or sanctions violations. Triggers Enhanced Due Diligence procedures.

name: Politically Exposed Person Risk
description: Risk category for customers identified as Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) or their close associates. Requires Enhanced Due Diligence due to elevated reputational and corruption risk.

name: Unclear Beneficial Ownership
description: Risk category triggered when the true beneficial owner or control structure of a customer entity cannot be clearly established. Requires Enhanced Due Diligence to identify and verify ultimate beneficial owners.

name: Unusual Transaction Pattern
description: Risk category identifying customers whose transaction behavior deviates from expected patterns or norms, potentially indicating money laundering, fraud, or other financial crime. Triggers Enhanced Due Diligence review.

name: Customer Complaint or Fraud History
description: Risk category for customers with documented history of complaints, fraud allegations, or previous suspicious activity. Requires Enhanced Due Diligence to assess ongoing risk.

name: Regulatory Concern
description: Risk category triggered when regulatory authorities or internal compliance functions identify specific concerns about a customer's activities or profile. Mandates Enhanced Due Diligence procedures.

name: Multiple Document Identity Verification
description: Control requiring collection and verification of multiple identity documents from high-risk customers as part of Enhanced Due Diligence. Strengthens identity verification beyond standard KYC procedures.

name: Beneficial Ownership Verification Control
description: Control mechanism for verifying and documenting the beneficial ownership structure of entity customers, ensuring transparency of ultimate beneficial owners.
context: Beneficial ownership verification (if customer is entity)

name: Source of Funds Verification Control
description: Control requiring verification and documentation of the origin and legitimacy of customer funds to prevent proceeds of crime from entering the banking system.

name: Enhanced Transaction Monitoring
description: Ongoing monitoring control applied to transactions of Enhanced Due Diligence customers to detect suspicious patterns, unusual activity, or potential financial crime.

name: Risk Assessment Documentation Control
description: Control requiring formal documentation and retention of risk assessments for Enhanced Due Diligence customers, creating an auditable record of compliance decisions and rationale.

name: Compliance Head
description: Senior compliance role responsible for approving Enhanced Due Diligence classifications and escalations. Acts as the final authority on EDD customer determinations.
context: Compliance Head approval required for EDD customers

name: High-Risk Customer
description: Customer classification for individuals or entities meeting one or more Enhanced Due Diligence trigger criteria, requiring enhanced verification, monitoring, and periodic review procedures.
context: Mandatory for high-risk customers and certain scenarios

Trigger Scenarios: Customer from high-risk country, PEP (Politically Exposed Person) identified, Beneficial ownership unclear, Transaction pattern unusual, Complaint or fraud history, Regulatory concern identified

name: Politically Exposed Person
description: Customer classification for individuals identified as Politically Exposed Persons or their close associates, requiring Enhanced Due Diligence procedures due to elevated compliance risk.

name: Enhanced Identity Verification
description: Enhanced KYC verification procedure requiring collection and verification of multiple identity documents for high-risk customers. Goes beyond standard identity verification to provide stronger assurance of customer identity.

name: Beneficial Ownership Verification
description: Enhanced KYC procedure for verifying the beneficial ownership structure of entity customers, ensuring transparency of ultimate beneficial owners as part of Enhanced Due Diligence.
context: Beneficial ownership verification (if customer is entity)

name: Source of Funds Verification
description: Enhanced KYC procedure requiring verification of the origin and legitimacy of customer funds, ensuring funds are not derived from illegal activities or sanctions violations.

name: Periodic EDD Review
description: Periodic review procedure for Enhanced Due Diligence customers conducted at minimum annually to reassess risk classification and verify continued appropriateness of enhanced procedures.

name: Ongoing Transaction Monitoring
description: Continuous AML screening procedure monitoring transactions of Enhanced Due Diligence customers to detect suspicious patterns, unusual activity, or potential financial crime indicators.

name: PEP Screening Policy
description: Policy governing the identification, screening, and ongoing monitoring of Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) and their family members and close associates. Establishes mandatory screening requirements at customer onboarding and continuous monitoring obligations, with escalation and enhanced due diligence procedures upon PEP identification.
context: PEP = Politically Exposed Person (government official, senior politician, military leader, etc.)
Screen all new customers against PEP databases
Ongoing monitoring for PEP status changes

name: Politically Exposed Person Risk
description: The financial crime risk posed by customers who are government officials, senior politicians, military leaders, or their immediate family members and close associates. This category encompasses the heightened risk of money laundering, corruption, and sanctions violations associated with PEP relationships.
context: PEP = Politically Exposed Person (government official, senior politician, military leader, etc.)

name: Mandatory PEP Screening at Customer Onboarding
description: Requirement to screen all new customers against PEP databases prior to account opening. This is a foundational control to identify high-risk customers at the point of relationship initiation.
context: Screen all new customers against PEP databases

name: PEP Family and Associate Screening
description: Requirement to screen not only direct PEPs but also their immediate family members and close associates against PEP databases. Extends the scope of PEP identification beyond the primary customer.

name: Ongoing PEP Status Monitoring
description: Requirement to continuously monitor existing customers for changes in PEP status throughout the customer lifecycle. Ensures that customers who acquire PEP status after account opening are identified and escalated.
context: Ongoing monitoring for PEP status changes

name: Enhanced Due Diligence for Identified PEPs
description: Requirement to conduct enhanced due diligence on any customer identified as a PEP. This mandatory escalation ensures deeper investigation of the customer's background, source of funds, and business purpose.

name: PEP Escalation to Compliance Head
description: Requirement to escalate any PEP identification to the Compliance Head for review and decision-making. Ensures senior management oversight of high-risk customer relationships.

name: Enhanced Ongoing Monitoring for PEPs
description: Requirement to apply enhanced ongoing monitoring to customers identified as PEPs. This elevated monitoring standard applies throughout the customer relationship to detect suspicious activity.

name: Transaction Restrictions for PEPs
description: Provision allowing for the consideration and implementation of transaction restrictions on PEP customers. Provides discretionary authority to limit or block certain transaction types based on risk assessment.

name: PEP Database Screening
description: Operational control mechanism for screening customers against PEP databases. Utilizes multiple data sources including FCA/PRA lists, sanctions cross-references, and third-party providers to identify PEP status.
context: Screen all new customers against PEP databases

name: PEP System Flagging
description: Control requiring that customers identified as PEPs be flagged in the bank's system. This flag serves as a persistent marker to alert staff and trigger enhanced procedures throughout the customer lifecycle.
context: Flag customer in system as PEP

name: PEP Screening
description: Anti-Money Laundering screening process for identifying Politically Exposed Persons and their family members and close associates. Includes initial screening at customer onboarding and ongoing monitoring throughout the customer relationship.
context: Screen all new customers against PEP databases
Ongoing monitoring for PEP status changes

name: Compliance Head
description: Senior compliance role responsible for receiving escalations of PEP identifications and making decisions regarding enhanced due diligence, ongoing monitoring, and transaction restrictions. Acts as the decision-making authority for high-risk PEP customer cases.

name: FCA/PRA PEP Lists
description: Official PEP databases maintained by the Financial Conduct Authority and Prudential Regulation Authority. These lists serve as primary sources for screening customers against known Politically Exposed Persons.

name: Sanctions List Cross-References
description: Regulatory sanctions lists used in conjunction with PEP screening to identify customers with sanctions exposure. Cross-referenced as part of the comprehensive PEP screening process.

name: New Customer
description: Customers applying for or opening new accounts with the bank. Subject to mandatory PEP screening as part of the customer onboarding process.
context: Screen all new customers against PEP databases

name: PEP Customer
description: Customer identified as a Politically Exposed Person, including government officials, senior politicians, military leaders, or their immediate family members and close associates. Subject to enhanced due diligence and ongoing monitoring.
context: PEP = Politically Exposed Person (government official, senior politician, military leader, etc.)
Flag customer in system as PEP

name: Adverse Media Screening
description: A screening process that checks all customers against news databases, third-party screening providers, and regulatory announcements to identify criminal convictions, fraud allegations, sanctions violations, and other adverse information. Findings are flagged for manual review and escalated to the Compliance Head if material to the banking relationship.
context: Screen all customers for adverse media (criminal convictions, fraud allegations, sanctions violations, etc.)
News databases, Third-party screening providers, Regulatory announcements
Flag for manual review, Assess materiality (relevance to banking relationship), If material: Escalate to Compliance Head, Consider account rejection or enhanced monitoring

name: Adverse Media Screening System
description: The operational control mechanism that screens all customers against news databases, third-party screening providers, and regulatory announcements to detect adverse media. Includes flagging, materiality assessment, and escalation procedures.
context: Screen all customers for adverse media (criminal convictions, fraud allegations, sanctions violations, etc.)
Sources: News databases, Third-party screening providers, Regulatory announcements

name: Sanctions Violation
description: The risk that a customer may be subject to or involved in sanctions violations, which is identified through adverse media screening as part of the bank's compliance obligations.
context: Screen all customers for adverse media (criminal convictions, fraud allegations, sanctions violations, etc.)

name: Fraud Allegation
description: The risk that a customer may have fraud allegations or be associated with fraudulent activity, which is identified through adverse media screening.
context: Screen all customers for adverse media (criminal convictions, fraud allegations, sanctions violations, etc.)

name: Criminal Conviction
description: The risk that a customer may have criminal convictions or a criminal history, which is identified through adverse media screening as part of customer due diligence.
context: Screen all customers for adverse media (criminal convictions, fraud allegations, sanctions violations, etc.)

name: Compliance Head
description: The role responsible for receiving escalations of material adverse media findings and making decisions regarding account rejection or enhanced monitoring.
context: If material: Escalate to Compliance Head
Consider account rejection or enhanced monitoring

name: Customer
description: All customers are subject to adverse media screening as part of the bank's compliance obligations to identify criminal convictions, fraud allegations, sanctions violations, and other adverse information.
context: Screen all customers for adverse media (criminal convictions, fraud allegations, sanctions violations, etc.)

name: Documentation and Record Retention Policy
description: Policy governing the collection, storage, access control, and retention of customer identity, verification, risk assessment, and screening records. Requires secure storage in a designated document management system with role-based access and comprehensive audit logging. Records must be retained for 6 years following account closure.
context: For each customer: Copy of identity document, Copy of address verification document, KYC verification record (date, method, approver), Risk assessment (if high-risk), PEP screening result, Adverse media screening result, AML screening result
Storage Location: Secure document management system (DMS-001)

name: Identity Document Collection and Storage
description: Mandatory requirement to collect and retain a copy of each customer's identity document as part of KYC documentation obligations.

name: Address Verification Document Collection and Storage
description: Mandatory requirement to collect and retain a copy of each customer's address verification document as part of KYC documentation obligations.

name: KYC Verification Record Documentation
description: Mandatory requirement to maintain a KYC verification record documenting the date, method, and approver for each customer verification performed.

name: Risk Assessment Documentation for High-Risk Customers
description: Mandatory requirement to document and retain a risk assessment for customers identified as high-risk.

name: PEP Screening Result Documentation
description: Mandatory requirement to retain documentation of PEP screening results for each customer.

name: Adverse Media Screening Result Documentation
description: Mandatory requirement to retain documentation of adverse media screening results for each customer.

name: AML Screening Result Documentation
description: Mandatory requirement to retain documentation of AML screening results for each customer.

name: Secure Document Storage in Designated System
description: Mandatory requirement to store all customer documentation and records in a secure document management system (DMS-001).
context: Storage Location: Secure document management system (DMS-001)

name: Role-Based Access Control for Records
description: Mandatory requirement to implement role-based access control restricting access to customer records to Compliance staff only.

name: Audit Trail Logging for Record Access
description: Mandatory requirement to maintain comprehensive audit logging of all access to customer records stored in the document management system.

name: Record Retention Period of Six Years Post-Account Closure
description: Mandatory requirement to retain all customer documentation and records for a minimum of 6 years following the closure of the customer's account.

name: Secure Document Management System
description: Designated secure system (DMS-001) for centralized storage of all customer documentation, identity records, verification documents, and screening results with built-in access controls and audit logging capabilities.
context: Storage Location: Secure document management system (DMS-001)

name: Role-Based Access Control System
description: Access control mechanism restricting document retrieval and viewing permissions to Compliance staff only, preventing unauthorized access to sensitive customer records.

name: Access Audit Logging
description: Automated logging mechanism that records all access events to customer records, enabling detection and investigation of unauthorized or suspicious access patterns.

name: Compliance Staff
description: Staff members with designated responsibility for accessing, managing, and maintaining customer documentation and records within the secure document management system. Only Compliance staff are authorized to access stored records.

name: Identity Document
description: Official identity document required to be collected and retained as part of KYC verification procedures for each customer. A copy must be stored in the secure document management system.

name: Address Verification Document
description: Document required to verify customer address as part of KYC procedures. A copy must be collected and retained in the secure document management system.

name: KYC Verification Record
description: Documented record of customer identity verification including the date of verification, the method used, and the staff member or system that approved the verification. Must be retained for 6 years post-account closure.

name: PEP Screening
description: Screening process to identify whether customers are classified as Politically Exposed Persons. Results must be documented and retained for 6 years post-account closure.

name: Adverse Media Screening
description: Screening process to identify adverse media coverage or negative information associated with customers. Results must be documented and retained for 6 years post-account closure.

name: AML Screening
description: Screening process to identify customers against sanctions lists and AML watchlists. Results must be documented and retained for 6 years post-account closure.

name: High-Risk Customer Classification
description: Risk category identifying customers assessed as high-risk, requiring enhanced due diligence and documented risk assessment records to be retained for 6 years post-account closure.

name: Customer Identification and Verification Policy
description: Policy governing exceptions and escalation procedures for non-standard customer identification scenarios, including refugees with limited documentation, foreign customers, high-value customers with complex structures, and politically exposed persons. Establishes mandatory escalation to Compliance Head for approval and alternative verification methods.
context: Customer Unable to Provide Standard Documents
Alternative verification: Notarized statement, passport alternative

name: Escalation for Customer Unable to Provide Standard Documents
description: Requires escalation to Compliance Head for approval when a customer cannot provide standard identification documents. Permits alternative verification methods including notarized statements and passport alternatives.
context: Customer Unable to Provide Standard Documents
Alternative verification: Notarized statement, passport alternative

name: Escalation for Foreign Customer with Limited UK Documentation
description: Requires escalation to Compliance Head when a foreign customer has limited UK documentation. Permits use of foreign equivalent documents supplemented with additional address verification.
context: Foreign Customer with Limited UK Documentation
Alternative: Foreign equivalent documents + additional address verification

name: Escalation for High-Value Customer with Complex Structure
description: Requires escalation to both Compliance Head and Legal review for high-value customers with complex ownership structures such as trusts or investment vehicles. Mandates beneficial ownership verification and enhanced due diligence.
context: Requirement: Beneficial ownership verification + enhanced due diligence

name: Escalation for Politically Exposed Person
description: Mandates escalation to Compliance Head for all politically exposed persons. Requires enhanced due diligence and senior approval before account opening or continuation.
context: Requirement: Enhanced due diligence, senior approval

name: Exception Documentation and Approval Process
description: Requires documentation of reasoning for exceptions, written approval from Compliance Head, recording of decision and rationale in system, and application of higher-risk monitoring.
context: Obtain written approval from Compliance Head
Record decision and rationale in system

name: Inadequate Customer Identification
description: Risk arising from customers unable to provide standard identification documents, including refugees and foreign nationals with limited documentation, creating potential gaps in KYC verification.
context: Customer Unable to Provide Standard Documents
Foreign Customer with Limited UK Documentation

name: Complex Beneficial Ownership
description: Risk associated with high-value customers holding accounts through complex structures such as trusts or investment vehicles, requiring verification of true beneficial owners.
context: Beneficial ownership verification + enhanced due diligence

name: Politically Exposed Person Risk
description: Risk posed by politically exposed persons requiring enhanced due diligence and senior management approval to mitigate reputational and regulatory exposure.
context: Requirement: Enhanced due diligence, senior approval

name: Compliance Head
description: Role responsible for approving exceptions to standard customer identification requirements, including cases involving refugees, foreign customers, complex structures, and politically exposed persons. Must provide written approval and ensure higher-risk monitoring is applied.

name: Legal Review Function
description: Role responsible for conducting legal review of high-value customers with complex ownership structures to verify beneficial ownership and assess compliance risk.
context: Requirement: Beneficial ownership verification + enhanced due diligence

name: Identity Verification for Non-Standard Scenarios
description: KYC verification process adapted for customers unable to provide standard documents, permitting alternative methods such as notarized statements and passport alternatives subject to Compliance Head approval.
context: Customer Unable to Provide Standard Documents
Alternative verification: Notarized statement, passport alternative

name: Address Verification for Foreign Customers
description: Enhanced address verification process for foreign customers with limited UK documentation, requiring additional verification beyond foreign equivalent documents.
context: Foreign Customer with Limited UK Documentation
Alternative: Foreign equivalent documents + additional address verification

name: Enhanced Due Diligence for Complex Structures
description: Enhanced due diligence process for high-value customers with complex ownership structures, including verification of beneficial ownership and legal structure review.
context: Requirement: Beneficial ownership verification + enhanced due diligence

name: Enhanced Due Diligence for Politically Exposed Persons
description: Enhanced due diligence process mandated for all politically exposed persons, requiring senior management approval and heightened ongoing monitoring.
context: Requirement: Enhanced due diligence, senior approval

name: Notarized Statement
description: Alternative identification document accepted for customers unable to provide standard documents, such as refugees with limited documentation.
context: Alternative verification: Notarized statement, passport alternative

name: Passport Alternative
description: Alternative to standard passport accepted for customers unable to provide conventional identification documents.
context: Alternative verification: Notarized statement, passport alternative

name: Foreign Equivalent Document
description: Foreign identification document accepted for foreign customers with limited UK documentation, supplemented with additional address verification.
context: Alternative: Foreign equivalent documents + additional address verification

name: Refugee Customer
description: Customer category with limited documentation requiring escalation to Compliance Head and alternative verification methods such as notarized statements.
context: Customer Unable to Provide Standard Documents

name: Foreign Customer
description: Customer with limited UK documentation requiring escalation to Compliance Head and use of foreign equivalent documents supplemented with additional address verification.
context: Foreign Customer with Limited UK Documentation

name: High-Value Customer
description: Customer with complex ownership structures such as trusts or investment vehicles requiring escalation to Compliance Head and Legal review, beneficial ownership verification, and enhanced due diligence.

name: Politically Exposed Person
description: Customer category requiring mandatory escalation to Compliance Head, enhanced due diligence, and senior approval. Subject to higher-risk monitoring.
context: Requirement: Enhanced due diligence, senior approval

name: Exception Documentation and Recording
description: Control requiring documentation of reasoning for exceptions, recording of Compliance Head approval, and retention of decision rationale in system for audit trail.
context: Obtain written approval from Compliance Head
Record decision and rationale in system

name: Higher-Risk Monitoring
description: Enhanced monitoring control applied to accounts approved through exception escalation process to mitigate compliance risk.

name: Branch Staff
description: Staff members working at bank branches responsible for customer-facing KYC processes, document collection, and initial compliance checks during account opening. They are accountable for accurate record-keeping and escalation of exceptions to management.
context: Collect required identity and address documents

name: Collection of Required Identity and Address Documents
description: Branch staff must collect required identity and address documents from customers as part of the KYC verification process during account opening.
context: Collect required identity and address documents

name: Physical Examination of Documents at Branch Opening
description: Branch staff must conduct physical examination of identity and address documents during the branch account opening process to verify authenticity and completeness.

name: Accurate Recording of Document Details
description: Branch staff must record all document details accurately in customer records to maintain compliance and audit trail integrity.

name: Escalation of Exceptions to Manager
description: Branch staff must escalate any exceptions or anomalies identified during document collection or examination to their manager for review and decision.

name: Maintenance of Customer Confidentiality
description: Branch staff must maintain customer confidentiality in all interactions and handling of personal and identity information collected during KYC processes.

name: Identity Verification
description: The process of verifying customer identity through collection and physical examination of required identity documents by branch staff during account opening.
context: Collect required identity and address documents

name: Address Verification
description: The process of verifying customer address through collection and examination of required address documents by branch staff during account opening.
context: Collect required identity and address documents

name: Branch Manager
description: Manager responsible for reviewing and deciding on exceptions escalated by branch staff during KYC document collection and verification processes.

name: Compliance Staff
description: Staff members responsible for executing compliance functions including KYC documentation review, application approval/rejection, PEP and adverse media screening, escalation management, and audit trail maintenance.

name: KYC Documentation Review
description: Compliance staff responsibility to review Know Your Customer documentation as part of the customer onboarding and verification process.

name: PEP Screening
description: Compliance staff obligation to conduct Politically Exposed Person screening as part of anti-money laundering controls.

name: Adverse Media Screening
description: Compliance staff obligation to conduct adverse media screening to identify reputational risks and potential financial crime indicators.

name: Audit Trail Maintenance
description: Compliance staff responsibility to maintain comprehensive audit trails documenting all compliance activities, decisions, and screening outcomes.

name: Application Approval or Rejection
description: Compliance staff must make explicit approval or rejection decisions on customer applications based on KYC documentation and screening results.

name: Escalation Management
description: Compliance staff responsibility to manage and escalate compliance issues, alerts, or exceptions through appropriate channels.

name: Compliance Head
description: Senior compliance role responsible for policy governance, exception management in high-risk scenarios, audit oversight, staff training delivery, and liaison with external regulators. The Compliance Head holds accountability for the bank's compliance framework and regulatory relationships.

name: Training and Awareness Policy
description: A policy establishing mandatory training obligations for all staff categories, covering KYC procedures, document verification, risk assessment, and regulatory compliance. The policy differentiates training frequency and content by role, with customer-facing staff receiving annual KYC training, compliance staff receiving quarterly updates with specialist training, and managers receiving annual policy overviews with escalation procedures.
context: All customer-facing staff: Annual KYC training
Compliance staff: Quarterly updates + specialist training
Managers: Annual policy overview + escalation procedures

name: Annual KYC Training for Customer-Facing Staff
description: Mandatory requirement that all customer-facing staff complete annual Know Your Customer training to ensure consistent application of KYC procedures and document verification standards.
context: All customer-facing staff: Annual KYC training

name: Quarterly Compliance Staff Updates and Specialist Training
description: Mandatory requirement that compliance staff receive quarterly updates supplemented with specialist training to maintain current knowledge of regulatory requirements and compliance procedures.
context: Compliance staff: Quarterly updates + specialist training

name: Annual Policy Overview and Escalation Procedures for Managers
description: Mandatory requirement that managers receive annual training covering policy overview and escalation procedures to ensure effective supervision and incident handling.
context: Managers: Annual policy overview + escalation procedures

name: Document Recognition and Authenticity Training
description: Training topic requirement covering staff competency in recognizing and verifying the authenticity of identity and address documents presented during customer onboarding and verification processes.

name: Acceptable Forms of Identity and Address Verification Training
description: Training topic requirement ensuring staff understand and can apply the bank's standards for acceptable identity and address verification methods during KYC procedures.

name: Risk Assessment Training
description: Training topic requirement covering staff competency in identifying, evaluating, and classifying customer and transaction risk to support compliance and fraud prevention objectives.

name: Escalation Procedures Training
description: Training topic requirement ensuring staff understand when and how to escalate compliance concerns, suspicious activities, and policy breaches to appropriate management and compliance functions.

name: Regulatory Requirements Training
description: Training topic requirement covering the regulatory framework and legal obligations applicable to the bank's operations, customer relationships, and compliance functions.

name: Customer Privacy Training
description: Training topic requirement ensuring staff understand customer privacy rights, data protection obligations, and confidentiality requirements in handling customer information.

name: Customer-Facing Staff
description: Staff members with direct customer interaction responsibilities who are required to complete annual KYC training and maintain competency in document verification, risk assessment, and escalation procedures.
context: All customer-facing staff: Annual KYC training

name: Compliance Staff
description: Staff members with compliance responsibilities who are required to receive quarterly updates and specialist training to maintain expertise in regulatory requirements and compliance procedures.
context: Compliance staff: Quarterly updates + specialist training

name: Managers
description: Management personnel responsible for supervision and oversight who are required to receive annual training on policy overview and escalation procedures to ensure effective incident handling and staff guidance.
context: Managers: Annual policy overview + escalation procedures

name: Know Your Customer Verification
description: The KYC verification process is a core compliance obligation covered extensively in staff training, encompassing document recognition, authenticity verification, and acceptable forms of identity and address verification.
context: All customer-facing staff: Annual KYC training

name: Customer Identity Verification Policy
description: A policy governing the mandatory verification of customer identity as a regulatory compliance requirement. The policy establishes that failure to verify customer identity constitutes a regulatory breach with significant external and internal consequences.
context: Failure to verify customer identity is a regulatory breach with potential consequences

name: Mandatory Customer Identity Verification
description: A mandatory requirement that customer identity must be verified as part of regulatory compliance obligations. Non-compliance with this provision triggers regulatory breaches and account closure.
context: Failure to verify customer identity is a regulatory breach with potential consequences

name: Financial Conduct Authority
description: The UK financial regulator with authority to impose regulatory fines for non-compliance with customer identity verification requirements.

name: Identity Verification Failure
description: The risk and compliance failure arising from the bank's inability or failure to verify customer identity, resulting in regulatory breach, reputational damage, and potential criminal liability.
context: Failure to verify customer identity is a regulatory breach with potential consequences

name: Customer Identity Verification Process
description: The operational process of verifying customer identity as mandated by regulatory requirements. Failure to execute this process results in regulatory fines, account closure, and potential criminal liability.
context: Failure to verify customer identity is a regulatory breach with potential consequences

name: All Staff
description: All bank staff members are accountable for compliance with customer identity verification requirements. Non-compliance by staff results in disciplinary action up to termination, performance management review, and loss of customer-facing roles.

name: Customer
description: A natural person subject to customer identity verification requirements. Non-compliant customers are subject to mandatory account closure.
context: Failure to verify customer identity is a regulatory breach with potential consequences

name: Customer Account
description: A customer account subject to identity verification requirements. Accounts of non-compliant customers are subject to mandatory closure as a regulatory consequence.

name: Annual KYC Procedure Testing
description: Annual testing of KYC procedures conducted by Internal Audit to verify compliance with KYC documentation standards and escalation handling protocols. This control ensures ongoing effectiveness of the KYC verification process.
context: Annual KYC procedure testing (see [[departments]] Internal Audit)
Sample testing of completed KYC files

name: KYC File Sample Testing
aliases: sample testing of completed KYC files
description: Internal Audit control involving sample testing of completed KYC files to verify compliance with documentation standards and assess the quality of KYC verification execution.
context: Sample testing of completed KYC files

name: Escalation Handling Review
description: Internal Audit control assessing the appropriateness of escalation handling within the KYC process, ensuring exceptions are managed according to policy requirements.

name: KYC Verification
description: Know Your Customer verification process subject to annual testing, sample file review, and regulatory examination. The process is measured against performance targets including 100% completion rate on account opening and average processing time of less than one business day.
context: Average KYC processing time | <1 business day

name: Internal Audit
